chapter: Chicago childhood: theaters, violin and first bass
title: The Monogram, comedians and Ralph Cooper's band at the Regal
summary: Hinton lists Chicago's lesser theaters and describes working in Ralph Cooper's band at the Regal Theater with Keg Johnson.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: That‟s right, that‟s exactly… and so the epitome of the two theaters there, was that it was the Dave Payton theater… Dave Payton at the Grand Theater and Erskine Tayback across the street at the Vind Dome Theater. Now of course the other subservient theaters, they had the Monogram, which was a comic place where they had all the comedians. Then we had…
What kind of comedians did they have in those days?
Marshall Garbage Rogers and [Unintelligible] just died. I worked for him in Chicago and…
Ralph Cooper. I worked in Ralph Cooper‟s ban in the Regal Theater.
Yeah, he had a band there.
Yeah, they were a team and then…
And then Leonard went… he did all the shows down in Atlantic City.
I know the guy you‟re talking about.
And Ralph Cooper‟s got the band.
What was his name, Leonard….well we can think of it later but, yeah, I know who you mean.

And then Ralph Cooper stayed at the Regal Theater and had a band because he was the MC. A good looking guy, the Cab Calloway type good looking, and light-complexioned guy, and they put him in charge of a band. Kay Johnson, Bird Johnson‟s brother was in the band, yours truly, I can‟t call the names of all of the guys. We played a little overture, the opening, and played for some singers and dancers, mostly a [unintelligible] was coming to the Regal Theater because that‟s where that revolution that I started to talk about… later Erskine Tate…
